plan: Jeremiah 51:15-19, 20-35, 36-44, 45-53, 54-58; 2 Kings 24:10-17; 2 Chronicles 36:10; 1 Chronicles 3:10-16; 2 Chronicles 36:11-14; Jeremiah 52:1-3a; 2 Kings 24:18-20a; Jeremiah 37:1-10

readings.title: The Portion of Jacob
readings.subtitle: The Maker of All vs. Worthless Idols
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 51:15] <dn>He</dn> made <dn>את</dn> the earth by <dn>His</dn> power, <dn>He</dn> established the world by <dn>His</dn> wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by <dn>His</dn> understanding.
[16] When <dn>He</dn> gives forth <dn>His</dn> voice the waters in the heavens roar, and <dn>He</dn> makes vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; <dn>He</dn> makes lightnings for the rain, and <dn>He</dn> brings the wind out of <dn>His</dn> treasuries.
[17] All mankind has become too brutish to know, every smith has been put to shame by the carved image, for his moulded image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
[18] They are worthless, a work of mockery. In the time of their punishment they perish.
[19] The Portion of Ya‛aqoḇ is not like them, for <dn>He</dn> is the Maker of all, and Yisra’ěl is the tribe of <dn>His</dn> inheritance. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is <dn>His</dn> Name.

readings.title: The Battle-Axe of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: Babylon's Destruction Foretold
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 51:20] <dq>“You are <dn>My</dn> battle-axe, weapons of battle, and with you <dn>I</dn> shall break nations in pieces, and with you <dn>I</dn> shall destroy reigns.</dq>
[21] <dq>“And with you <dn>I</dn> shall break in pieces the horse and its rider, and with you <dn>I</dn> shall break in pieces the chariot and its rider.</dq>
[22] <dq>“And with you <dn>I</dn> shall break in pieces man and woman, and with you <dn>I</dn> shall break in pieces old and young, and with you <dn>I</dn> shall break in pieces the young man and the maiden.</dq>
[23] <dq>“And with you <dn>I</dn> shall break in pieces the shepherd and his flock, and with you <dn>I</dn> shall break in pieces the farmer and his yoke of oxen. And with you <dn>I</dn> shall break in pieces governors and rulers.</dq>
[24] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall repay Baḇel and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for <dn>את</dn> all the evil they have done in Tsiyon before your eyes,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[25] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am against you, O destroying mountain, who destroys all the earth,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall stretch out <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> hand against you. And <dn>I</dn> shall roll you down from the rocks, and make you a burnt mountain.</dq>
[26] <dq>“And they shall not take from you a stone for a corner nor a stone for a foundation, but you shall be a waste forever,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[27] Lift up a banner in the land, blow a shophar among the nations! Prepare the nations against her, call the reigns together against her: Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a commander against her, bring up horses like hairy locusts.
[28] Separate the nations against her, with the sovereigns of the Medes, its governors and all its rulers, all the land of his rule,
[29] so that the land shakes and writhes in pain. For every plan of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be established against Baḇel, to make <dn>את</dn> the land of Baḇel a ruin, without inhabitant.
[30] The mighty men of Baḇel have ceased to fight, they remained in their strongholds. Their might has failed, they became like women, they have burned her dwelling places. The bars of her gate have been broken.
[31] One runner runs to meet another, and one reporter to meet another, to report to the sovereign of Baḇel that his city is taken on all sides,
[32] and the fords have been captured, and <dn>את</dn> they have burned the reeds with fire, and the soldiers are startled.
[33] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“The daughter of Baḇel is like a threshing-floor at the time it is trodden. Yet a little while and the time of her harvest shall come.”</dq>
[34] “Neḇuḵaḏretstsar the sovereign of Baḇel has devoured us, he has crushed us, he has made us an empty vessel, he has swallowed us up like a monster. He has filled his stomach with my delicacies, he has driven us away.
[35] “Let the violence done to me and my flesh be upon Baḇel,” says the inhabitant of Tsiyon. And, “Let my blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea,” says Yerushalayim.

readings.title: The Desolation of Babylon
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Pleads Zion's Case
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 51:36] Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am pleading <dn>את</dn> your case. And <dn>I</dn> shall take <dn>את</dn> vengeance for you and dry up <dn>את</dn> her sea and make her fountain dry.</dq>
[37] <dq>“And Baḇel shall become a heap, a habitation of jackals, an astonishment and a hissing, without inhabitant.</dq>
[38] “Together they roar like lions, they shall growl like lions’ cubs.
[39] <dq>“In their heat <dn>I</dn> prepare <dn>את</dn> their feasts. And <dn>I</dn> shall make them drunk, so that they rejoice, and sleep a neverending sleep and not awake,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[40] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with male goats.</dq>
[41] <dq>“Oh, how Shěshaḵ has been captured, the praise of all the earth been seized! How Baḇel has become a ruin among the nations!</dq>
[42] <dq>“The sea has risen over Baḇel, she has been covered with the roaring of its waves.</dq>
[43] <dq>“Her cities have become a ruin, a dry land and a desert, a land where no one dwells, neither does son of man pass by it.</dq>
[44] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall punish Běl in Baḇel. And <dn>I</dn> shall make him spew out <dn>את</dn> what he has swallowed, and nations shall no longer stream to him. Even the wall of Baḇel shall fall.</dq>

readings.title: Escape the Judgment
readings.subtitle: A Report of Violence, Ruler Against Ruler
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 51:45] <dq>"Come out of her midst, <dn>My</dn> people! And let everyone deliver <dn>את</dn> his being from the burning displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[46] <dq>“And lest your heart grow faint, and you fear the report heard in the land – for a report shall come one year, and after that, in another year a report shall come, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler –</dq>
[47] <dq>therefore see, the days are coming that <dn>I</dn> shall bring punishment on the carved images of Baḇel, and all her land shall be put to shame, and all her slain fall in her midst.</dq>
[48] <dq>“And the heavens and the earth and all that is in them shall shout for joy over Baḇel, for the ravagers shall come to her from the north,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[49] As Baḇel is to fall for the slain of Yisra’ěl, so for Baḇel the slain of all the earth shall fall.
[50] You who have escaped the sword, go away! Do not stand still! Remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> from afar, and let Yerushalayim come to your heart.
[51] We are ashamed because we have heard reproach. Shame has covered our faces, for strangers have come into the set-apart places of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[52] <dq>“Therefore see, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that <dn>I</dn> shall bring punishment on her carved images, while the wounded groan throughout all her land.</dq>
[53] <dq>“Though Baḇel should mount up to the heavens, and though she should make the height of her strength inaccessible, ravagers shall come to her from <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Sound of Destruction
readings.subtitle: The Broad Walls of Babylon Demolished
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 51:54] Listen! A cry from Baḇel, and great destruction from the land of the Kasdim,
[55] because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is ravaging <dn>את</dn> Baḇel, and shall silence her loud voice. And her waves shall roar like great waters, the noise of their voice shall resound,
[56] because the ravager shall come against her, against Baḇel, and her mighty men shall be captured. Every one of their bows shall be broken, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is the <dn>Ěl</dn> of recompense, <dn>He</dn> shall certainly repay.
[57] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make her rulers drunk, and her wise men, her governors, and her deputies, and her mighty men. And they shall sleep a lasting sleep, and not awake,”</dq> declares the Sovereign, whose Name is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts.
[58] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“The broad walls of Baḇel are completely demolished, and her high gates are burned with fire, and peoples labour in vain, and the nations weary themselves for fire.”</dq>

readings.title: The Siege of Jerusalem
readings.subtitle: King Jehoiachin Exiled to Babylon
readings.text:
[2 Kings 24:10] At that time the servants of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sovereign of Baḇel came up against Yerushalayim, and the city was besieged.
[11] And Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sovereign of Baḇel came against the city, as his servants were besieging it.
[12] And Yehoyaḵin sovereign of Yehuḏah, and his mother, and his servants, and his heads, and his eunuchs went out to the sovereign of Baḇel. And the sovereign of Baḇel, in the eighth year of his reign, took <dn>את</dn> him prisoner.
[13] And he took from there <dn>את</dn> all the treasures of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the treasures of the sovereign’s house, and he cut in pieces <dn>את</dn> all the objects of gold which Shelomoh sovereign of Yisra’ěl had made in the Hěḵal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said.
[14] And he exiled <dn>את</dn> all Yerushalayim, and <dn>את</dn> all the officers and <dn>את</dn> all the mighty brave men – ten thousand exiles – and all the craftsmen and smiths. None remained except the poorest people of the land.
[15] And he exiled <dn>את</dn> Yehoyaḵin to Baḇel. And <dn>את</dn> the sovereign’s mother, and <dn>את</dn> the sovereign’s wives, and <dn>את</dn> his eunuchs, and <dn>את</dn> the leading men of the land he exiled from Yerushalayim to Baḇel.
[16] And <dn>את</dn> all the mighty brave men, seven thousand, and craftsmen and smiths, one thousand, all who were strong and fit for battle, these the sovereign of Baḇel brought to Baḇel into exile.
[17] And the sovereign of Baḇel set up <dn>את</dn> Mattanyah, Yehoyaḵin’s uncle, to reign in his place, and changed <dn>את</dn> his name to Tsiḏqiyahu.

readings.title: Jehoiachin Taken to Babylon
readings.subtitle: The Valuable Utensils of the House of YeHoVaH are Plundered
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 36:10] And at the turn of the year Sovereign Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sent and brought him to Baḇel, with the valuable utensils from the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and made <dn>את</dn> Tsiḏqiyahu, Yehoyaqim’s brother, sovereign over Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim.

readings.title: The Genealogy of the Kings of Judah
readings.subtitle: From Solomon to the Sons of Josiah
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 3:10] And Shelomoh’s son was Reḥaḇ‛am, Aḇiyah his son, Asa his son, Yehoshaphat his son,
[11] Yoram his son, Aḥazyahu his son, Yo’ash his son,
[12] Amatsyahu his son, Azaryah his son, Yotham his son,
[13] Aḥaz his son, Ḥizqiyahu his son, Menashsheh his son,
[14] Amon his son, Yoshiyahu his son.
[15] And the sons of Yoshiyahu: Yoḥanan the first-born, the second Yehoyaqim, the third Tsiḏqiyahu, the fourth Shallum.
[16] And the sons of Yehoyaqim: Yeḵonyah his son and Tsiḏqiyah his son.

readings.title: The Reign of Zedekiah
readings.subtitle: He Did Not Humble Himself Before YeHoVaH
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 36:11] Tsiḏqiyahu was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim.
[12] And he did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn>. He did not humble himself before Yirmeyahu the prophet, who spoke from the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[13] And he also rebelled against Sovereign Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar, who had made him swear by <dn>Elohim</dn>, but he stiffened <dn>את</dn> his neck and hardened <dn>את</dn> his heart against turning to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl.
[14] Also, all the heads of the priests and the people trespassed more and more, according to all the abominations of the nations, and they defiled <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had set apart in Yerushalayim.

readings.title: Zedekiah's Evil Reign
readings.subtitle: He Rebelled Against the Sovereign of Babylon
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 52:1] Tsiḏqiyahu was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Ḥamutal the daughter of Yirmeyahu of Liḇnah.
[2] And he did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to all that Yehoyaqim had done.
[3] For through the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> this came to be against Yerushalayim and Yehuḏah, until <dn>He</dn> had cast <dn>את</dn> them out from <dn>His</dn> presence. And Tsiḏqiyahu rebelled against the sovereign of Baḇel.

readings.title: Zedekiah Appointed by Babylon
readings.subtitle: His Reign and Rebellion
readings.text:
[2 Kings 24:18] Tsiḏqiyahu was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Ḥamutal the daughter of Yirmeyahu of Liḇnah.
[19] And he did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to all that Yehoyaqim did.
[20] For this took place in Yerushalayim and Yehuḏah because of the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, until <dn>He</dn> had cast <dn>את</dn> them out from <dn>His</dn> presence. And Tsiḏqiyahu rebelled against the sovereign of Baḇel.

readings.title: Zedekiah Seeks Counsel from Jeremiah
readings.subtitle: A Prophecy of Jerusalem's Inevitable Fall
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 37:1] And Sovereign Tsiḏqiyahu son of Yoshiyahu reigned instead of Konyahu son of Yehoyaqim, whom Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel set up to reign in the land of Yehuḏah.
[2] But neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land had listened to the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> spoke by the prophet Yirmeyahu.
[3] And Tsiḏqiyahu the sovereign sent <dn>את</dn> Yehuḵal son of Shelemyah, and <dn>את</dn> the priest, Tsephanyahu son of Ma‛asěyah, to the prophet Yirmeyahu, saying, “Please pray to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> for us.”
[4] Now Yirmeyahu was still coming and going among the people, for they had not yet put him in prison.
[5] Meanwhile, Pharaoh’s army had set out from Mitsrayim. And when the Kasdim who were besieging Yerushalayim heard <dn>את</dn> news of them, they withdrew from Yerushalayim.
[6] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yirmeyahu the prophet, saying,
[7] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘Say this to the sovereign of Yehuḏah, who sent you to <dn>Me</dn> to inquire of <dn>Me</dn>, “See, Pharaoh’s army which has come up to help you, shall turn back to Mitsrayim, to their own land.</dq>
[8] <dq>“And the Kasdim shall return and fight against this city, and take it and burn it with fire.” ’</dq>
[9] <dq>“Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘Do not deceive <dn>את</dn> yourselves, saying, “The Kasdim shall go away from us,” for they do not go.</dq>
[10] <dq>For though you had stricken <dn>את</dn> the entire army of the Kasdim who are fighting against you, and there remained only wounded men among them, they would get up, each man in his tent, and burn the city with fire.’ ”</dq>
